anchors.100: Accurate grammar across long turns; wording sounds like a fluent speaker chatting, not a textbook.
anchors.70: Minor slips that never block meaning; mostly natural wording with some translated-sounding phrases.
anchors.40: Frequent errors or stiff, word-for-word phrasing that makes the listener work to follow.
anchors.10: Errors so severe that most turns are hard to understand.

anchors.100: Carries the conversation: develops every answer with reasons, examples, or a short story, asks questions back, and moves the topic forward without being prompted.
anchors.70: Answers with some detail and occasionally asks back or adds a new thread, but often waits for the partner's next question.
anchors.40: Mostly minimal answers to the partner's questions; rarely adds detail, asks back, or brings anything new.
anchors.10: One-to-three-word replies only; the conversation depends entirely on the partner.

anchors.100: Speaks in connected multi-sentence turns with natural linkers (because, so, but, actually, anyway) and few restarts.
anchors.70: Can hold a turn for two or three sentences with some hesitation or restarts.
anchors.40: Turns are short and choppy; long pauses or abandoned sentences are common.
anchors.10: Cannot sustain more than a fragment at a time.

anchors.100: Understands each question, answers what was actually asked, and self-corrects or asks for clarification naturally when needed.
anchors.70: Mostly follows and answers logically, with occasional missed nuance or weak repair.
anchors.40: Often answers a different question or guesses instead of checking meaning.
anchors.10: Cannot follow the exchange or build a coherent reply.
